published_statement: p.6, Sec. 3: 'The mode functions for a free scalar field of mass mu are U_k(x) = [(2 pi)^n 2 w_k]^{-1/2} e^{ik.x}, w_k = sqrt(|k|^2+mu^2) (3.1) ... The quantum inequality (2.12) becomes  rho-bar >= -(1/2pi) INT_0^oo dw INT d^n k/(2 pi)^n w_k |(f^{1/2})^(w + w_k)|^2 = -(C_n/2pi) INT_0^oo dw INT_mu^oo dw' w'^2 (w'^2-mu^2)^{n/2-1} |(f^{1/2})^(w+w')|^2 (3.2), where C_n is equal to the area of the unit n-1-sphere divided by (2 pi)^n, i.e. C_n = 1/(2^{n-1} pi^{n/2} Gamma(n/2)) (3.3).' [pi's restored; text layer shows '1/2', '(2)^n', 'C_n/2'.] With (2.12) (p.5): rho-bar >= -(1/pi) INT_0^oo dw SUM_lambda (w_lambda^2/|g_tt| + (1/4) grad_i grad^i)|U_lambda|^2 |(f^{1/2})^(w+w_lambda)|^2, and (2.9) f^(w) = INT dt f(t) e^{-iwt}. p.7: (3.4) rho-bar >= -(C_n/(2pi(n+1))) INT_mu^oo du |(f^{1/2})^(u)|^2 u^{n+1} Q_n(u/mu); 'massless fields in ... four dimensions with the sampling function (1.1) ... the present bound is 9/64 of Ford and Roman's result.'
published_hypotheses: n+1-dimensional globally static spacetime, ds^2 = -|g_tt(x)| dt^2 + g_ij dx^i dx^j, timelike Killing vector d_t (p.3, (2.1)); for (3.2) specifically Minkowski space, |g_tt| = 1
free, real scalar field of mass mu >= 0 (p.3, (2.2)); (3.2) holds for any mu >= 0 and any spatial dimension n
a complete orthonormal set of positive-frequency modes f_lambda = U_lambda e^{-i w_lambda t} (p.3, (2.3)); in Minkowski the plane waves (3.1) with normalisation [(2 pi)^n 2 w_k]^{-1/2}
sampling function f: smooth, non-negative, sufficiently rapid decay, NOT necessarily even (p.3); the sampler enters as |(f^{1/2})^(w+w_k)|^2 integrated over w in (0,oo), with f^ as in (2.9)
the bounded quantity is the time-averaged NORMAL-ORDERED energy density, in the Fock space built on the static vacuum, measured by a static observer (p.3)

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for (3.2): there is NO empirical datum in this result. (3.2) is a theorem of free scalar QFT in Minkowski space (canonical commutation relations + convolution theorem + a pointwise inequality (A.2)); its only inputs are the mode normalisation (a convention fixed by the CCR) and the sampler class. In 1998 the authors lacked later FRAMEWORK results -- Hadamard-state generality, the absolute QEI (Fewster-Smith 2007), local covariance (Fewster-Pfenning 2006) -- and every one of these, READ here at the two/three restating sites, reproduces the same Minkowski form with the same 1/(16 pi^3) (math-ph/0501073 eq.7, gr-qc/0702056 eq.88) or its Parseval equivalent (2003.01815 eq.61). Evidence therefore runs AGAINST 'lacked data changes the conclusion' for this result: nothing moved, and the one discrepancy found (a factor pi) is the TREE's transcription loss from a PDF text layer, not an error in the 1999 paper -- the paper's own 9/64 claim is reproduced exactly with its printed factor.
grade_evidence: F&T (3.2), READ at source (alphaXiv page text, pp.3-7), is re-derived from (3.1)+(2.12): radial reduction and C_n symbolic for n = 1..6 (T3), change of variables to (3.4)/(3.5) numerically (T4), (2.18) re-derived (T5), and the paper's printed '9/64 of Ford and Roman' reproduced exactly (T6b); three later papers restate the same form (T8). Hypotheses as the tree uses them (massless, n = 3, plane waves with norm 2) are a specialisation inside the published scope, and the tree's route-2 solve returns the correct RATIO (2.12)/(3.2). RECORDED DISCREPANCY, NOT A REFUTATION OF ANYTHING: the tree's quotation of (3.2) as '-(1/2) INT ...' (fewsterteo.py:29-30, 465) drops a 1/pi lost from the PDF text layer; with the printed 1/(2 pi) the same solve gives P = 1/pi, the printed literal prefactor of (2.12). So PREFACTOR_212 = 1 (fewsterteo.py:23, 153; ledger.py:1806) is exact only as the pi-relative normalisation both routes share (T2c), and the sentence 'nothing here trusts the text layer' (fewsterteo.py:34-35) is not true of the (3.2)/(2.10) readings. No downstream number moves -- PREFACTOR_212 is only printed, and every numeric use of the family carries the pi (T7). Not NARROWED: no published hypothesis the tree's route 2 needs is dropped (the smooth-sampler hypothesis bears on the owner's OTHER uses, sec. 1(c)/2, and is recorded as OPEN there). Not WRONG: the external result is reproduced, and a transcription loss is a discrepancy. Nothing depends on a moved datum.
